dataset: Montgomery County CXR (lung-field segmentation, chest X-ray)
eval_note: 138 images, no official split (often reported with JSRT + Shenzhen as a 3-dataset lung-seg suite). Lung-field Dice is nearly saturated (~0.98 fully supervised), so the interesting comparison is LOW-LABEL semi-supervised. No credible fully-unsupervised lung-field baseline exists (pre-deep-learning atlas/registration methods reach ~0.94). Scores compiled from papers/abstracts - verify in source.

papers.name: A semi-supervised multi-connection contrastive learning framework for x-ray lung segmentation based on mutual distillation
papers.authors: Zeng X, Abdulla N, Liang B, Alwesabi OA, Sumari P
papers.model_size: Inference/deployed model = ~1.15M-param lightweight student (4 conv layers 1->16->32->64->128 + U-Net decoder), 75.2 MB, 0.963 GFLOPs. TRAINING uses a ResNet-50 'teacher' (~25M+) + student + discriminator + projection heads (no combined total reported). The 0.96 Dice is the student result. (Our EncoderDecoder was ~133M params in the run observed.)
papers.teacher_training: NOT Mean-Teacher / EMA - 'teacher' is a misnomer. It's peer co-training / mutual learning: ResNet-50 model and 1.15M student trained simultaneously by gradient descent. Teacher losses: (1) supervised seg loss on the ~2 labels (sees GT directly, same as student), (2) bidirectional mutual pseudo-label / contrastive loss with the student (student teaches teacher too), (3) mid-level encoder-feature cosine consistency, (4) adversarial loss from a discriminator. Fully end-to-end, no pretraining phase. => NO hidden supervision: teacher's only GT signal is the same 2 labels; comparison is fair on the supervision axis.
papers.pretraining: NONE for the headline numbers - encoder is randomly initialized, trained 500 epochs from scratch. No ImageNet, no SAM/foundation model, no external labeled data. The contrastive/self-supervised stage runs only on the same dataset's own unlabeled X-rays. (An ImageNet-pretrained variant is tested as a secondary experiment but not the reported result.) Authors: 'This framework does not require any pre-training, and the labels are only for preventing model collapse'. => clean low-supervision baseline, fair to compare against.
papers.protocol: 138 Montgomery images; label set of M images (only these have GT) + rest. NO validation set. Labeled counts M are LITERAL image counts, not fractions. Unlabeled pool = all remaining images. TEST SET = those same remaining images (transductive eval, e.g. M=2 -> 2 labeled + 136 unlabeled, tested on the 136). Same M across Montgomery/JSRT/Shenzhen. 95% CI over 20 from-scratch runs, seed 1234567. Self-contained per dataset (no cross-dataset train/test).
papers.why_relevant: Extreme low-label lung segmentation on Montgomery specifically - the most direct comparison for our small-labeled-fraction setting.
papers.caveat: NOT directly comparable to our numbers: (a) 128x128 vs our 256x256 - low res inflates Dice on big structures like lung fields; (b) transductive eval (test images = the unlabeled training pool) vs our held-out 70/15/15 split; (c) M is a literal image count, not a fraction. Rough mapping to our 97-image Montgomery train pool: labeled_fraction ~0.02 -> ~2 labeled, ~0.10 -> ~10, ~0.21 -> ~20. Treat their Dice as an optimistic reference.
papers.score_confidence: verified from paper full-text (values are 95% CIs over 20 runs)
